name: MATP (cream / pearl)
summary: The dilution locus - one gene, five alleles (Cr, prl, sun, sno, N). One cream copy is a partial dilution (palomino / buckskin / smoky black); two cream, or cream beside any of the three recessives, is a full double dilute. Pearl needs two copies for a milder uniform dilution; sunshine needs two and reads like champagne; snowdrop needs two and is indistinguishable from a double cream. That last part is the point: a horse that looks like a cremello may carry one cream allele or none, and only its genotype says which.

phenotypes.name: Pearl carrier
phenotypes.description: One pearl copy does nothing on its own - the horse looks undiluted and only its descendants show it. Breeding two carriers is how classic pearl appears.

phenotypes.name: Dilution carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy of sunshine or snowdrop, and nothing to see. Both are recessive and both look exactly like a horse carrying neither - which is how the first snowdrop foal was born pale out of two apparently undiluted parents.

phenotypes.name: Single cream
phenotypes.description: Red cut hard and black cut a little - palomino on a chestnut, buckskin on a bay, smoky black on a black. The points go dark brown, never jet black.

phenotypes.name: Classic pearl
phenotypes.description: Black cut hard and red barely touched - a warm, lightened coat that keeps its colour rather than washing out. Only two pearl copies and no cream produce it.

phenotypes.name: Sunshine
phenotypes.description: Two sunshine copies. A whole-coat dilution that reads closer to champagne than to a cremello - warm and light rather than washed out - and, unlike the double dilutes, it does not give the horse a pale blue eye.

phenotypes.name: Double dilute
phenotypes.description: Red almost entirely gone and black heavily cut - cremello, perlino or smoky cream, a near-white body over rusty points. Two cream copies do it, and so does one cream with one pearl.
